# `az.pdf()` {#fn-az-pdf}

**Verified on 2.0.9006.** Periodic azimuth densities passed the fine-grid and wide-width D01 checks. [D01 rerun](d01-density-checks.qmd).

**Validation on 2.0.9005.** The analytic density checks in D01 found a folding error near north at 0.005-degree spacing and omitted periodic tails in the two 100-degree-width cases. [D01 results](d01-density-checks.qmd).

[Function index](function-index.html#idx-az-pdf)

```{=html}
<p>Azimuth is circular. Curves wrap across north before the density-height
cutoff is applied. For an asymmetric triangle, the clockwise arc from <code>lower</code>
to <code>upper</code> must include <code>az</code> and be shorter than a full turn.
For example, limits 358 and 3 enclose a mode of 0. For the four new families,
the field interval (including both cosine tapers, if used) spans at most one
turn. An aperture convolved with Gaussian survey error can still have tails
across the full circle. The grid starts at zero and ends before 360. Each
measurement is retained separately. Trimming does not renormalise the stored
ordinates. Choose a grid fine enough to resolve the narrowest shoulder.
</p>
```

[Field examples and comparison of all six profiles](orientation-densities.qmd#measurement-families).

<details><summary>Method references</summary>

```{=html}
<p>Silva, F (2020) A probabilistic framework and significance test for the analysis of structural orientations
in skyscape archaeology <em>Journal of Archaeological Science</em> 118, 105138. \Sexpr[results=rd]{tools:::Rd_expr_doi("10.1016/j.jas.2020.105138")}
</p>



```

</details>

**Interpretation and limits.** A reported uncertainty enters differently as the standard deviation of a normal density and as the half-width of a uniform density. Record which interpretation the measurement supports before combining sites.


<details><summary>Implementation arguments, return value and documented modes</summary>

```{=html}
<table><thead><tr><th>Argument</th><th>Formal default</th><th>Behaviour in this interface</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><th scope="row"><code>az</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>True bearings clockwise from north, in degrees. For triangular, the preferred bearing (mode).</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>unc</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>One width or one per observation. Standard deviation for normal,
outer half-width for uniform, Epanechnikov or symmetric triangular, and core
half-width for tapered uniform or uniform convolved with normal. Omit when
supplying triangular limits. See 'Choosing a measurement model'.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>pdf</code></th><td><code>&quot;normal&quot;</code></td><td><p>One measurement family per call. See 'Choosing a measurement model'
for all six names. The default is <code>"normal"</code>. The historical abbreviations
<code>"n"</code> and <code>"u"</code> are accepted and names are case-insensitive.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>name</code></th><td>—</td><td><p>Optional labels in the same order as the measurements.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>.res</code></th><td><code>0.01</code></td><td><p>Spacing of the output bearing grid in degrees. Default 0.01.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>.cutoff</code></th><td><code>1e-05</code></td><td><p>Minimum density retained on the output grid. Default <code>1e-5</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>verbose</code></th><td><code>TRUE</code></td><td><p>Logical. Display progress or informational messages. Default <code>TRUE</code>.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>taper</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>Outer extension on each side of a tapered uniform core, in degrees.
Required for <code>"tapered_uniform"</code>. Zero gives a uniform density.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>survey.sd</code></th><td><code>0.5</code></td><td><p>Standard deviation of independent bearing or declination
error, in degrees, for <code>"uniform_normal"</code>. Defaults to 0.5 degrees per observation. Zero gives a uniform density.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>lower</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>The two bounding directions of a triangular model, in degrees.
Supply both and omit <code>unc</code>. Each bound, <code>taper</code> and <code>survey.sd</code>
may be a scalar or a vector in measurement order.</p></td></tr><tr><th scope="row"><code>upper</code></th><td><code>NULL</code></td><td><p>The two bounding directions of a triangular model, in degrees.
Supply both and omit <code>unc</code>. Each bound, <code>taper</code> and <code>survey.sd</code>
may be a scalar or a vector in measurement order.</p></td></tr></tbody></table><h5>Return value</h5><p>A skyscapeR.pdf list. The data component contains one data frame per measurement, in input order, with azimuth x in degrees and density y. The metadata record the measurements, names, uncertainties, distribution type and numerical settings.
</p>
```

</details>
